docs.title: 🚗 Autoware 3D SLAM & Navigation
docs.text: This section introduces the full workflow for RobiX/RobiS robots using the Autoware open-source autonomous driving framework with 3D LiDAR SLAM, waypoint recording, and cruise control.

docs.title: 1. Launch the Autoware Navigation Stack
docs.text: roslaunch ros_robot_control ros_robot_control.launch

docs.title: 2. Start the RViz-Based Navigation GUI
docs.text: rosrun robot_rviz_16 robot_rviz_16

docs.title: 3. Configure RViz Display Parameters
docs.text:
Use the following config file: 

~/catkin_ws/src/slam_app/ros_qt5_gui_app_rviz_16_en/default.yaml

docs.title: 4. Connect to Upper Computer
docs.text:
• Default main node: 127.0.0.1
  • Local IP: 127.0.0.1
  • Click Connect
  • If failed, restart the upper computer and try again

docs.title: 5. Start Point Cloud Recording
docs.text:
Click Start Pointclouds Record in the interface and drive the robot using the remote.

⚠️ Do not reverse or use erratic patterns like S-turns. Maintain a smooth and forward-only path.

Once done, stop recording.

docs.title: Option 1 — via RViz (not recommended):
docs.text: Use Publish Point to draw points manually.

docs.title: Option 2 — preferred:
docs.text: After finishing point cloud recording, click Start Trajectory Recording. The recorded path will reflect actual movement and is fully drivable.

docs.title: 7. Start Mapping + Trajectory Recording Together
docs.text:
1. Click Start Trajectory Recording
  2. Then click Start Mapping
  3. Wait until terminal output finishes (Duration stops updating)
  4. Stop recording — mapping completes automatically

docs.title: 8. Activate Navigation
docs.text:
1. Drive the robot to the initial point used during point cloud recording
  2. Click Start Navigation
  3. Switch to RViz tab
  4. Wait for map to load

If positioning seems off, use 2D Pose Estimate in RViz to manually align.

docs.title: 9. Enable Trajectory Cruise
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Status tab
  2. Click Enable Trajectory Cruise

Behavior: - Robot follows the path - Stops at the endpoint - If clicked again, will reverse the path

💡 If started at endpoint, the robot will go: end -> start -> end

If trajectory loop is enabled, the car will loop: 

start → end → U-turn → end → start → U-turn → ...

Ensure enough space for U-turns.

docs.title: 10. Start Waypoint Follower
docs.text:
⚠️ Robot will start immediately when this mode is activated.

  • Set the robot to remote control mode first
  • Ensure safety and environment clearance
  • Press emergency stop if needed

❗ Navigation and tracking modes cannot run at the same time. Turn off navigation first.

Use 2D Pose Estimate to initialize pose if needed.

docs.title: Obstacle Handling
docs.text:
• Robot stops for obstacles only in the red box detection zone
  • Obstacle must not be too close (<0.2m blind zone)
  • Robot resumes 2 seconds after the obstacle moves away

docs.title: 🤖 Introduction to RobiS and RobiX Robots
docs.text: Welcome to the RobiS and RobiX robot documentation. These robots are designed for research, education, and autonomous mobility scenarios with different configurations and onboard capabilities.

docs.title: 🎮 Remote Control Setup for RobiS Robot
docs.text:
This section describes how to use the remote controller to operate your RobiS robot. Remote control system includes a onboard receiver and a PS2 joystick remote controller, they both have red and green indicator lights.

The joystick button description

docs.title: 🔌 Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
Power On

Turn on the robot by pressing the power button.

Switch on the controller

Both solid red and green lights indicate a successful connection.

Unlock Remote Control Mode

Every time after turning on the robot power, remote control needs to be unlocked. - Press the Mode button. - Then press START to activate remote control mode.

Controls Overview

Button/Joystick Function Mode Wake up / exit sleep START Enter remote control mode Left joystick Move robot forward/backward Right joystick Rotate robot left/right L1 Increase speed (max 1.5 m/s) L2 Decrease speed (min 0) Remote Indicator Flashing = pairing, Solid = connected

💡 Other buttons currently have no assigned function.

docs.title: 🛑 Sleep Mode
docs.text:
• If unused for 5 minutes, the controller enters sleep.
  • To wake it up, press the Mode button then press Start to unlock.

docs.title: ⚠️ Usage Precautions
docs.text:
• Ensure the remote controller receiver is plugged into the robot.

  • Install batteries with correct polarity.

  • When using multiple robots, match them one-by-one to avoid cross-control.

  • The maximum communication distance between the remote control and the car is 8 meters; please do not exceed this range.
  • During the mapping process, it is recommended to tap the L2 button to reduce the remote control speed. The slower the mapping speed, the more accurate the positioning will be.

docs.title: 🖥️ Remote Login (NoMachine)
docs.text: Remotely access the RobiS robot using the built-in NoMachine server.

docs.title: ✅ Default Credentials
docs.text:
• Username: robify
  • Password: robify1234 (also used for sudo)

docs.title: 🔗 Standard Connection Steps
docs.text:
1. Install NoMachine on your computer: https://downloads.nomachine.com/

  2. Skip the corresponding operation steps according to the instructions, check them, and click OK in sequence.

  3. The navigation car is equipped with the corresponding NoMachine remote software (Arm8 architecture) at the factory. When the car is connected to the same LAN as the computer (mandatory), the SSH service of the current York car will be automatically displayed on the following interface. Double click to proceed.

  4. Next, if you reinstall the NoMachine server, confirm to regenerate the SSL certificate, and select OK. Not skipped.

  5. Login with: Username: robify Password: robify1234

  6. Then you will see some tutorial instructions for some tools, skip the corresponding operation steps according to the instructions, check them, click OK in sequence, and wait to enter the system.

docs.title: Issue: Multiple Robots Detected
docs.text:
1. Click Edit Connection

  2. Set correct IP manually. Port: 4000, Protocol: NX

  3. Use ifconfig on the robot to check IP address.

  4. After switching IP, connecting again will prompt for IP address change. Select [OK]

docs.title: Issue: Certificate Expired
docs.text:
Reinstall NoMachine on the robot:

sudo apt-get remove nomachine-enterprise-desktop
sudo dpkg -i nomachine_8.16.1_1_arm64.deb

Make sure the .deb file is in the correct directory.

🧠 Tip: If the touch screen is unresponsive on first login, press Enter before typing the password.

docs.title: 🚀 1. Start Autoware open-source navigation program
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh # launch docker

Inside docker execute:

 <video controls width="600">
   <source src="../../imgs/camera.mp4" type="video/mp4">
 </video>

docs.title: 🖥️ 2. Launch navigation upper computer
docs.text:
source slam_app/devel/setup.bash
rosrun robot_rviz_16 robot_rviz_16

docs.title: ⚙️ 3. Configure rviz display parameters
docs.text: slam_apps/src/ros_qt5_gui_app_rviz_16_en/default.yaml

docs.title: 🔗 4. Upper computer connection (auto-connected by default)
docs.text: Master node IP is 127.0.0.1, local IP is 127.0.0.1, then click Connect. If connection fails, close and restart the upper computer, then connect again. (This process is auto-connected by default.)

docs.title: 📹 5. Start Pointclouds Record
docs.text: After clicking “Start Pointclouds Record”, use the remote controller to drive the vehicle once around the area to be mapped (no need to drive back and forth). Note: the subsequent trajectory recording will be the path you just drove, so avoid backward motion or any motion the vehicle cannot perform autonomously, e.g. reversing or sharp S-turns. Record the actual position and orientation of the vehicle. When point-cloud recording is finished, stop it.

docs.title: 📍 6. Start Waypoint Saver
docs.text: After point-cloud recording is complete, start Waypoint Saver. The recorded trajectory will be the drivable path the vehicle just followed.

docs.title: 🗺️ 7. Start Mapping & Waypoint Saver
docs.text: First start Waypoint Saver, then start Mapping, and wait until the control-node terminal output stops (the Duration time is finished). Then stop Waypoint Saver. Mapping will stop automatically when finished.

docs.title: 🧭 8. Start Navigation
docs.text: Manually drive the vehicle back to the starting position and orientation used when point-cloud recording began, click “Start Navigation”, switch the interface to [rviz], and wait a moment for the map to load automatically (larger maps take longer). If localization is incorrect you can set the initial pose with rviz’s 2D Pose Estimate; then drive a short distance to let the map and laser points re-align automatically—this process is called re-localization. (When the colorful laser points roughly coincide with the white feature points, the algorithm will automatically match the robot’s position.) You can set a target pose with rviz’s 2D Nav Goal. Ensure navigation localization is correct, set the target pose, and switch the chassis to upper-computer control mode with the remote; the chassis will then navigate to the target pose.

docs.title: 🔁 9. Start Cruise Trajectory
docs.text: Return to the [Status] page and click “Start Cruise Trajectory”; the vehicle will follow the trajectory on the map. When encountering obstacles the vehicle will detour; on reaching the end it will stop automatically. Click “Start Cruise Trajectory” again and the vehicle will make a U-turn and drive back to the start. (After clicking “Start Navigation” the algorithm resets the order; cruise always starts from the beginning, so if the first time you start cruise the vehicle is at the end, the sequence will be: end→start→end again—hence the emphasis on driving back to the start first.) If the vehicle is not at the start or end when cruise is started, the algorithm will find the nearest trajectory point and drive to the start or end along the closest segment. If “Loop Trajectory” is checked before starting cruise, the vehicle will loop indefinitely: start→end→U-turn→end→start→U-turn. (Ensure sufficient space for U-turns at start and end; obstacle avoidance only guarantees the vehicle itself will not collide—external accessories are not protected.)

docs.title: 🛤️ 10. Start Waypoint Follower
docs.text:
Warning: the vehicle will move immediately upon starting Waypoint Follower; always set the remote controller to manual mode first, ensure the surrounding area is safe before switching to upper-computer/navigation mode on the remote (or press the emergency stop beforehand and ensure safety before starting). Navigation and Waypoint Follower cannot run simultaneously; first ensure “Stop Navigation”. Waypoint Follower must be started from the pose where point-cloud recording began, or you can set the initial pose with rviz’s 2D Pose Estimate.

During following, the vehicle can only stop in front of obstacles; only Cruise Trajectory can detour. Stop range:

Obstacles within the red box can trigger stopping, but they must not be too low nor too close to the LiDAR (0.2 m blind zone); the LiDAR filters out data too close to itself. In stop-mode, the vehicle will automatically resume 2 s after the obstacle is removed.

Please refer to the accompanying video.

docs.title: 🧭 Cartographer 2D Mapping and Navigation
docs.text: RobiS supports the Cartographer SLAM algorithm developed by Google. Cartographer offers higher mapping accuracy and integrated localization, but it requires more computational power.

docs.title: 🔧 1. Launch device driver
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh   # start docker

Inside docker run:

source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch robot_start robot_start.launch

docs.title: 🗺️ 2. Start Cartographer 2-D laser mapping (new terminal)
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh   # start docker

Inside docker run:

source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch robot_start carto_2d_mapping.launch

docs.title: 👀 3. Open rviz visualization (new terminal)
docs.text:
rviz

Load the preset:

/home/robify/catkin_ws/src/robot_start/rviz/cartographer_2d_mapping.rviz

Drive the robot in manual mode until the map is complete.

docs.title: 💾 4. Save the map (new terminal)
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh   # start docker

Inside docker run:

source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
sh catkin_ws/src/robot_start/sh/save_map.sh

After saving, stop the Cartographer mapping terminal (Ctrl-C).

docs.title: 🧭 5. Launch navigation
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh   # start docker

Inside docker run:

source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch robot_start teb_navigation_slam.launch

docs.title: 🎯 6. Open rviz for navigation (new terminal)
docs.text:
rviz

Load the preset:

/home/robify/catkin_ws/src/robot_start/rviz/cartographer_2d_navigation.rviz

After setting pose with 2D Pose Estimate, use 2D Nav Goal to click any spot for point-to-point navigation (switch remote to upper-computer mode).

Please refer to the accompanying video.

docs.title: 🛠️ Initialization of chassis and sensor drivers
docs.text: Before using other functions of the RobiS robot, it's necessary to activate essential hardware modules such as the chassis drive, LiDAR, and IMU.

docs.title: 🚀 Start Docker
docs.text:
run the following command:

./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch my_control run_device_only.launch

You can view the corresponding data by subscribing to mec_car. 

./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
rostopic echo /mec_car

docs.title: 🧩 Start Drivers Individually
docs.text: If you need to start each component separately, use the following commands in separate terminals:

docs.title: 📹Depth Camera Sensor
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch astra_camera astra_pro.launch

Open a new terminal, type rviz and press Enter. In the lower-left corner, click “Add”, choose “By topic”, and select the camera image topic corresponding to your camera.

After adding, you can see the camera information in the lower-left corner. In the topic displayed under “Image”, you can choose among depth information, RGB image, and infrared data.

docs.title: 🔄 LiDAR Sensor
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch vanjee_lidar_sdk start.launch

On the right-hand side, select the display Type for the point-cloud data and change it to XYOrbit to view it as a 3-D point cloud.

docs.title: 📡 IMU Sensor
docs.text:
roscore
./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
rosrun TransducerM_pkg TMSerial

You can view the corresponding data by subscribing to robot_imu.

rostopic echo /robot_imu

docs.title: 🧭 Chassis driver
docs.text:
./autoware.ai/open.sh
source catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
roslaunch ros_mec_msg ros_mec_msg.launch

After starting, you can publish motion-control topics to make the robot move forward, backward, etc., as shown below

rostopic pub /cmd_vel [tab] [tab]   #Press the Tab key twice and modify the linear velocity (x-axis speed).

💡 Tip: You need to confirm that the remote control is in "上位机" (host-computer) mode and that the emergency stop has been released.

Once the drivers are active, you can proceed to 2D mapping, navigation, or autonomous operations.

Please refer to the accompanying video.
